name: GAPS
description: Gaps is a single-player patience game in which four rows are arranged in suit sequence from 2 through King. Four gaps are created by removing the aces, and cards can move only into legal next-rank same-suit gaps.

content.text: Gaps is a single-player patience game in which four rows are arranged in suit sequence from 2 through King. Four gaps are created by removing the aces, and cards can move only into legal next-rank same-suit gaps.
Gaps belongs to the Montana family of patience games and appears in 20th-century rule collections under names including Montana and Spaces.
One player. Gaps is a patience (solitaire) game; a single player plays alone and makes all decisions about which cards to move into gaps and when to redeal.
One shuffled deck and table space for four rows of thirteen cards.
Deal all 52 cards face up into four rows of thirteen. Remove all four aces, leaving four empty spaces.

items.text: Addiction: Same core play but typically allows three redeals rather than two.
No-shuffle Redeal: Unsorted cards are redealt without shuffling, reducing randomness and changing solvability.
Unlimited Redeals: Redeals continue until solved; turns game into a deterministic endurance variant.
